excerpt: Responsibilities Network AI Strategy and Leadership • Develop and lead KIPP's multi-year, network-wide AI strategy, aligned to One KIPP and the KIPP 2030 Plan, that positions the network for the next generation of teaching, learning, and operations; bring it through the AI Working Group and keep it current as the field moves.
description:
Responsibilities

Network AI Strategy and Leadership

  • Develop and lead KIPP's multi-year, network-wide AI strategy, aligned to One KIPP and the KIPP 2030 Plan, that positions the network for the next generation of teaching, learning, and operations; bring it through the AI Working Group and keep it current as the field moves.

  • Serve as the AI expert for the entire KIPP Foundation and the go-to advisor for regions, the Schools team, and Foundation leadership on AI tools, uses, and risks.

  • Own KIPP's position on instructional AI and the standard the network uses to judge whether a tool serves its students; propose and maintain the network's AI decision structure, making clear how recommendations reach decision-makers and how decisions flow to Foundation teams and regions.

  • Translate the strategy so it travels: a regional superintendent can repeat it in a sentence, a development officer can put it in front of a funder, and a school leader recognizes it in the guidance they receive.

AI Pilot Leadership and Measurement

  • Manage the AI pilot group, setting its priorities and the standard of evidence for AI pilots across the Foundation and regions.

  • Design and administer the measurement system for AI pilots: go to regions to assess pilot quality, collect, and analyze evidence, and produce a report on each pilot that states clearly whether the tool is working and for which students.

  • Partner with the Schools team, which oversees instructional pilots, and with external researchers to set the comparison design, subgroup breakouts, and data plan before licenses are issued.

  • Apply a common evaluation framework to every AI tool under consideration, covering efficacy and alignment to One KIPP anchor metrics; accessibility for multilingual learners, students with IEPs, and students arriving below grade level; bias and equity risk; implementation requirements and total cost of ownership; and student data privacy and security, with the Data and Technology team setting technical, privacy, and security requirements.

AI Recommendations and Partnerships

  • Serve as the final recommender on AI vendors, uses, and approaches for both Foundation and regional work, including work led by the Schools team, where the Chief Schools Officer makes the final decision.

  • Make scale, continue, or stop recommendations grounded in pilot data, and present them to the AI Working Group and senior leaders with the evidence behind them.

  • Identify, negotiate, and steward partnerships with research and development partners, a small set of key vendors, and university researchers; structure agreements so partners build to KIPP's model, and lead structured diligence with the Data and Technology team on any platform under consideration.

  • Help Foundation teams use AI more effectively in their own work, keeping the principles for the Foundation's internal AI use and the standard for classroom tools in one coherent position.

Network Coordination Across Regions

  • Coordinate AI work across KIPP regions, maintaining a current inventory of tools, cost, funding source, early outcomes, lessons learned, and privacy considerations through regional AI leads and touchpoints such as RAMP, so the Foundation can answer a question about network AI use the week it is asked.

  • Advise regions on how tools fit KIPP's approach and what evidence the network needs to recommend them, respecting regional leaders' authority over their own schools.

  • Broker multi-region pilots with a shared challenge, a common evaluation design, and a clear division of labor, so the network learns once instead of many times and reduces duplicate spending.

Funding, Ecosystem, and External Voice

  • Build KIPP's relationships with funders investing in AI in education and, with the Development team, position KIPP to attract the philanthropic dollars and support its priority AI work needs, coordinating regional and national requests so KIPP does not compete with itself.

  • Represent KIPP at the conferences, convenings, and forums where AI tools, funding, and policy take shape, and keep Foundation leaders current on the ecosystem through a weekly read to the CEO.

  • Own the strategic narrative and evidence base the Development team carries externally, with the CEO holding final say on what goes out, and prepare the AI Working Group's updates to the KIPP Foundation Board.

  • Carry what pilots teach into national guidance and the annual One KIPP planning cycle.

Skills and Mindsets

  • Mission and Student Focus: Demonstrates passion and commitment to KIPP’s mission and possesses the desire and ability to uphold KIPP’s core values (Focus on Excellent Results, Collective Impact, and Courageous Action)

  • Self Management: Demonstrated record of setting ambitious goals and achieving them with consistency. Invests in developing teammates' skills and mindsets to address gaps in achieving team growth; determines what quantitative and qualitative data are most relevant to their goals and supports the team in creating and monitoring systems for collecting, reviewing, and acting upon data to drive outcomes; able to monitor progress, communicating status to the right stakeholders and adjusting plans and use of time to ensure systems are yielding desired outcomes.

  • Work Management: Sets a clear vision for new or complex bodies of work. Develops and implements agile project plans, navigating difficult situations or conflicts while maintaining effective relationships with all stakeholders; creates and ensures systems are in place for knowledge management.

  • Process Management: Able to build and align goals and project plans with organization priorities; leverages relevant organizational processes and systems to execute work; can build and maintain knowledge management systems; effectively develops and codifies cross-team processes relevant to their team's work that improve work quality and efficiency; uses data to drive process improvements in support of organizational priorities.

  • Data-Driven Actions and Decisions: Efficiently defines the right metrics to evaluate work and ensures critical team actions, decisions, and recommendations are driven by data; effectively works with team to resolve issues around data to ensure sound data-informed decisions.

  • Communication and Change Management: Effectively articulates case for change through clear and compelling presentations and translates this into actionable plans. Effectively tailors communications and engagement approach for different audiences to deepen investment and drive actions and behavior change that would lead to org-wide goals. Acts as a champion for change with cross-team stakeholders.

  • Collaboration: Has the interpersonal, diplomatic, relationship building, and communications skills needed to develop successful working relationships with diverse constituents to deliver results. Evolves and adapts plans and approach with diverse stakeholders to drive results. Possesses excellent communication skills with aptitude for translating complex information into clear and persuasive narratives that convince others by identifying benefits for all.

  • AI Expertise and Evaluation: Brings deep, current expertise in AI tools and a working understanding of what these systems can and cannot do. Able to evaluate AI products against instructional goals, evidence of efficacy, accessibility, bias and equity risk, and student data privacy requirements, and to design measurement systems that show whether a tool is working and for which students.

Experience and Qualifications

  • 7-10+ years of professional experience, including 5+ years in K-12 education, with progressive leadership responsibility in complex, mission-driven organizations; bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, advanced degree preferred.

  • Deep, current expertise in AI and its uses in education, with the credibility to advise school leaders, system leaders, and senior executives on what these tools can and cannot do.

  • Experience teaching or leading in schools serving students like those KIPP serves, with the classroom judgment to tell a tool that works from a tool that demos well.

  • Proven record of leading strategy or major initiatives across a school system, charter management organization, or multi-region network, including aligning senior leaders and teams without direct authority.

  • Demonstrated experience designing measurement or evaluation systems for programs or pilots that others continued to run, including working with research partners on comparison designs, subgroup breakouts, and data plans, and turning results into clear recommendations.

  • Proven record of negotiating and managing partnerships with vendors, research organizations, or universities, with working knowledge of student data privacy, FERPA, and operating across multiple state regulatory environments.

  • Experience building relationships with funders or securing philanthropic support preferred; experience with budget ownership and vendor contract management a plus.

Work Conditions

  • Basic Travel Expectations: Up to 10% (up to 20 days per year)

  • Full time, Exempt

Location

It is preferred, but not mandatory for this role to be based out of a KIPP Foundation office. This role has the option of working from a remote office full-time. KIPP Foundation offices are in NYC and Chicago.

Compensation and Benefits

In compliance with local law, we are disclosing the compensation, or a range thereof, for roles in locations where legally required. Actual salaries will vary based on several factors, including but not limited to external market data, internal equity, and relevant experience. The salary range for this position is $156,000-$188,500. In addition, KIPP Foundation provides a variety of benefits to employees, including: 

  • 25 holidays for + 18 days additional flexible PTO days (flexible PTO increases to 23 days for years 3 and 4 and to 28 days for years 5+).

  • 100% paid parental leave

  • 100% coverage of the premium for employee and 75% for employee + family’s medical/dental/vision plans.

  • Wellness benefits such as fitness reimbursements, discounted tickets to theme parks/attractions, backup care support for children and adults/elders, and our employee assistance program

  • Finance Security benefits include such as a 401K retirement plan with 4% match, employer-sponsored legal plans, life/disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts

About the Organization

KIPP Public Schools is a national network of tuition-free public charter schools that prepares students with the skills and confidence to create the future they want for themselves, their communities, and us all. We are a network of 279 schools, nearly 16,500 educators, and nearly 210,000 students and alumni.

Our mission: Together with families and communities, we create joyful, academically excellent schools that prepare students with the skills and confidence to pursue the paths they choose—college, career, and beyond—so they can lead fulfilling lives and build a more just world.

Our vision: Every child grows up free to create the future they want for themselves and their communities.

The KIPP Foundation is a nonprofit organization that supports KIPP public charter schools across the country. The KIPP Foundation helps to develop outstanding educators to lead KIPP schools; provides tools and resources for excellent teaching and learning; promotes innovation; and facilitates the exchange of insights and ideas across KIPP and other public schools and organizations.

About Our Values:

Excellent Results for Students: We value results over effort and know that our work is not finished until all students thrive. We maintain high expectations for self, team, and students. We drive outcomes by operating with agility, removing barriers, differentiating support, and prioritizing student-centered solutions—especially for those at the margins.

Collective Impact: We are one team. We win together. We embody a one-team mindset by working collaboratively across teams, aligning goals, and leveraging the strengths of all teammates. We build trust-based relationships and ensure inclusive decision-making by engaging those closest to the work. We provide clarity through simple, repeatable systems and goals that enable transformational outcomes.

Courageous Action: Our belief in what we can achieve is unwavering, fueling our optimism and commitment to overcome any challenge. We demonstrate an unwavering belief in students' potential and a commitment to addressing systemic inequities. We approach challenges with resilience, a solutions-focused mindset, and adaptability. We foster a psychologically safe environment centered on trust and accountability where feedback is encouraged. We leverage data to reflect on progress, own setbacks, celebrate successes, and continuously improve to maximize impact.

title: Senior Identity Governance Engineer
excerpt: Ready to be a Titan? At ServiceTitan, we are building a next-generation identity fabric, and this role engineers the governance layer on top of it.
description:
Ready to be a Titan?

At ServiceTitan, we are building a next-generation identity fabric, and this role engineers the governance layer on top of it. Identity spans cloud environments, SaaS applications, data systems, machine identities, and now AI agents, which makes it one of the most sprawling attack surfaces in the enterprise. You will make sure every identity, whether a Titan, a third-party contractor, a service account, or an AI agent, has the right access, for the right reason, at the right time, and that we can prove it.


Corporate Engineering (IT) administer our identity platforms, including Okta and Lumos, and run lifecycle operations. InfoSec defines identity governance requirements and validates that controls work. You sit in InfoSec and engineer the governance layer: authentication and authorization design standards, entitlement models, access review automation, and audit-ready evidence. You administer Veza with Corporate Security, Security Architecture, Product Security, and Security Operations, work with Corporate Engineering and System Owners to put governance requirements into practice, and you will be a key owner of our ISPM and IGA program.


What you'll do:

You engineer identity governance: the tooling, automation, and design standards that make access reviewable and provable. Corporate Engineering and IT administer the identity platforms, and InfoSec GRC owns the policies and the review program.

  • Access Request Governance: Define governance requirements and design patterns for access request workflows across privileged systems (code repositories, databases, infrastructure), including role-based, time-bound, delegated, and just-in-time access, and measure adoption so access is not granted outside the governed workflow. Corporate Engineering and IT administer Lumos and implement the workflows; you specify the requirements, build the monitoring that detects bypass, and validate that they work.
  • Authentication & Authorization Design: Partner with Security Architecture to define authentication and authorization design standards (SSO, MFA and phishing-resistant requirements, OIDC/SAML/SCIM patterns, least-privilege role models) for enterprise tools, and review integrations against them.
  • Authorization Governance & Entitlement Design: Provide the technical design for authorization decisions on job functions and privileged data access, including critical systems such as ST Admin roles, Snowflake, Salesforce, and other high-risk entitlements. Build role models scoped to job function and normalize entitlement data across applications in Veza so access can be reviewed like for like.
  • Access Review & Lifecycle Automation: Build and operate the tooling and automation behind the user access review program (SOX ITGC, PCI DSS, SOC 1/2, ISO 27001), which InfoSec GRC owns, and behind joiner/mover/leaver control assurance, including leaver access-reversion evidence, reconciliation against the authoritative HR source, and orphaned account detection.
  • Privileged Access Governance: Build visibility into standing privileged access across core cloud infrastructure and the data platform and drive it down, moving toward time-bound elevation (PIM and JIT) with governed exceptions for the access that must remain.
  • Identity Fabric Architecture: Define the target-state governance architecture across Okta, Veza, and Lumos and the risk-based identity lifecycle it supports. You administer Veza in combination with Corporate Security, Security Architecture, Product Security, and Security Operations, building its data source integrations, policies, and alerts. Corporate Engineering and IT administer Okta and Lumos, and you partner with them on lifecycle and workflow integration.
  • ISPM & Continuous Governance: Add continuous monitoring to periodic certifications. Build identity analytics that detect over-privileged accounts, shadow identities, dormant access, and identity drift, and automate remediation workflows with named owners.
  • Non-Human Identity & AI Security: Build the inventory and governance workflows for service accounts, API keys, personal access tokens, and AI agents, including ownership, rotation, and attestation requirements, and drive remediation with owning teams. Ensure AI integrations are covered by rigorous entitlement management, in partnership with our AI governance review process.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with Corporate Engineering, the administrative owner of identity platforms and lifecycle operations, alongside Security Architecture and System Owners to ensure every enterprise tool is integrated with identity by design, while InfoSec GRC defines identity governance requirements and validates control effectiveness.
  • Compliance as Code & Audit Support: Provide the technical identity evidence for audit requests (SOX, PCI, ISO 27001, SOC 1/2), partnering with our SOX IT compliance team, who coordinate with auditors. Automate evidence collection so compliance is a byproduct of good engineering, not a manual chore.
  • Vendor Engagement: Partner with Corporate Engineering to engage our strategic identity vendors (Veza, Okta, Lumos). Hold vendors accountable to their commitments and service levels, influence their product roadmaps, and secure the implementation and adoption support we need to maximize our return on investment.

What you'll bring:

We are looking for deep identity experience, whether in governance, administration, engineering, or a mix of these, paired with hands-on technical skills. You build the tools that make governance work.

  • The Fundamentals: 5+ years in identity and access, with depth in Identity Governance & Administration. Broader experience in identity and access engineering (SSO, provisioning, directory or identity platform automation) is welcome alongside a governance background. You deeply understand lifecycle management (Joiner/Mover/Leaver), RBAC/ABAC and entitlement modeling, Separation of Duties, privileged access governance, and the Principle of Least Privilege, and you can design and automate access certification programs at enterprise scale.
  • The Modern Stack: Hands-on experience with modern IGA and identity discovery tools (e.g., Veza for authorization graphs and entitlement visibility, Lumos for SaaS governance and access requests, Okta for lifecycle orchestration and identity governance workflows). Experience administering an authorization graph platform such as Veza is especially valuable, since you will own it in partnership with other security teams.
  • Authentication & Authorization Design: Working knowledge of authentication and authorization standards and patterns (SSO, OIDC, SAML, SCIM, MFA, RBAC/ABAC) and the ability to review enterprise integrations against them.
  • NHI Governance: Proven experience governing non-human identities (service accounts, API keys, workload identities) in cloud-native environments (AWS/GCP), including inventory, ownership assignment, rotation and expiry requirements, periodic attestation, and risk exception handling. You can read cloud IAM and secrets management configurations and partner with the engineering teams who operate those platforms.
  • Security Posture: Understanding of ISPM principles, including detecting identity drift, excessive entitlements, orphaned accounts, and misconfigurations before they are exploited, and turning those findings into governed remediation.
  • Compliance Fluency: Ability to translate regulatory and audit requirements (SOX ITGC, PCI DSS, SOC 2, ISO 27001) into identity controls, automated workflows, and audit-ready evidence. You are comfortable working directly with internal and external auditors.
  • Automation & Engineering Skills: Proficiency in a scripting language (e.g., Python or Go), plus API integration experience and familiarity with workflow or low-code tooling, to automate access reviews, evidence collection, and remediation tracking.

Who You Are

  • A Systems Thinker: You understand the balance between People, Process, and Technology. You don't just fix a ticket; you fix the process that created the ticket.
  • An Enabler of Innovation: You believe security should be a tailwind, not a headwind. You build identity governance that lets Titans move faster and collaborate safely.
  • Data-Driven: You use identity analytics to find high-risk areas and prioritize work based on actual risk data.

Why This Role Matters

As ServiceTitan scales and integrates AI across our platform, identity governance is what keeps access defensible. Your work protects customer data, supports the trust our customers place in us, and lets our teams move faster with confidence.

Be Human With Us:
Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. We need amazing people like you to help us challenge the conventional and think differently about the problems that we’re solving. We’re in this together. Come be human, with us.


Use of AI Technology:

We use technology, including automated and AI-assisted tools, to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools are designed to improve efficiency and enhance the candidate experience. AI tools are not used to make hiring decisions; all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams.


What We Offer:

When you join our team, you’re not just accepting a job. You’re making a career move. Here’s how we’ll support you in doing some of the most impactful work of your career:

  • Flextime, recognition, and support for autonomous work: Flexible time off with ample learning and development opportunities to continue growing your career. We offer a comprehensive onboarding program, leadership training for Titans at all levels, and other programs and events. Great work is rewarded through Bonusly, peer-nominated awards, and more.
  • Holistic health and wellness benefits: Company-paid medical, dental, and vision (with 100% employer paid options and 90% coverage for dependents), FSA and HSA, 401k match, and telehealth options including memberships to One Medical.
  • Support for Titans at all stages of life: Parental leave and support, up to $20k in fertility services (i.e. IUI and IVF), surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement, on demand maternity support through Maven Maternity, free breast milk shipping through Maven Milk, pet insurance, legal advisory services, financial planning tools, and more.

description:
Fully Remote — South Africa | Independent Contractor | Full-Time, UK office hours | A UK domiciliary care provider

About the Role

Outsource Ability is recruiting on behalf of a UK domiciliary care provider for an experienced and organised Rostering Coordinator. The provider delivers approximately 2,000 hours of home care each week across around 90 care staff.

You will plan, maintain and adjust care workers' schedules so that client visits are covered consistently, staff availability is used effectively and travel between visits is practical. This is not a data-entry role. It requires independent judgement and active problem-solving across a two-week rolling rota.

This role covers rostering only. You will not change assessed care needs, reduce agreed care durations or decide that a required visit can be missed. Unresolved staffing and care-delivery risks must be escalated to the designated line manager.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain the two-week rolling rota, keeping regular clients with the same care worker wherever practical.
  • Complete the following week's rota each Monday to Tuesday, recording leave, sickness and visit changes accurately.
  • Monitor and resolve uncovered visits, which can exceed 100 during busy periods, by reorganising runs and contacting staff for additional availability.
  • Use bank staff and pickup arrangements for short-term and weekend cover rather than permanent runs.
  • Plan runs using full client postcodes, allowing practical travel time between visits.
  • Allocate work within each care worker's availability and contracted hours, avoiding over-allocation or double-booking.
  • Assess new care packages against geography, visit times and staff capacity, working to the Wednesday cut-off for Monday starts.
  • Keep the rostering system accurate and handle client and staff information confidentially.
  • Escalate uncovered visits and operational risks to the designated line manager, with a summary of action taken.

Systems

  • CareFree (or a similar care-scheduling platform)

Experience with every system is not essential, but you must be confident learning new technology.

What We're Looking For

Essential

  • Demonstrable experience coordinating high-volume schedules, staff rotas, dispatch or comparable logistics work.
  • Ability to solve multi-step scheduling problems and see how one change affects other visits, staff and routes.
  • Excellent accuracy and numerical confidence when tracking staff hours, gaps and deadlines.
  • Clear written and spoken English, with confidence contacting staff and updating UK colleagues remotely.
  • Sound decision-making under pressure, with the judgement to escalate an unresolved visit promptly.
  • Confident use of scheduling software.
  • Ability to work securely with confidential information.

Advantageous

  • Experience in domiciliary care, healthcare or another time-critical visiting service.
  • Experience using CareFree or a similar care-scheduling platform.
  • Familiarity with UK postcodes, local route planning and two-week repeating rota patterns.

Remote Work Requirements

Applicants must:

  • Be based in South Africa.
  • Have a modern laptop or PC with an Intel i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 processor or equivalent and a minimum of 8GB RAM.
  • Have a stable fibre connection with a minimum of 50 Mbps download and 50 Mbps upload.
  • Have a functional UPS, inverter or power station able to run the router and laptop for a minimum of 2–4 hours during load shedding.
  • Have a professional noise-cancelling headset with a clear microphone.
  • Have a quiet workspace suitable for calls and video meetings.
  • Be available for the agreed full-time hours during UK office times.

excerpt: About Re:Build At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America.
description:
About Re:Build

At Re:Build, our mission is to ensure the next generation of important products are made, at scale, in America. We are laying the foundation for a better future for our customers, employees, and communities by revitalizing America's manufacturing base and creating meaningful jobs across the country, including in historically deindustrialized regions.

We operate a sophisticated, end-to-end manufacturing platform that partners with industrial companies and innovators to take products from first concept to full-scale production in critical verticals including aerospace and defense, electrification, medical, energy and environment, and robotics and automation.

The way we operate is as important as the work we do. It's guided by The Re:Build Way, 16 principles that shape how we collaborate with each other, partner with our customers and vendors, and contribute to the communities where we operate. (link to The Re:Build Way principles)

Who we are looking for

We're looking for an experienced process excellence practitioner who has actually built the kind of processes that teams use — not ones that get drafted, launched, and quietly abandoned. You've spent 7-10+ years deep in commercial operations, GTM operations, or process excellence, and you've learned through hands-on experience that the gap between a well-designed process and a forgotten one usually comes down to adoption, documentation, and continuous reinforcement. You know Lean principles—process flow analysis, consistent procedures, cause investigation, and PDCA—not as theory but as tools you use daily. You are comfortable applying them in a commercial, non-manufacturing context.

What sets you apart is that you treat AI as a working instrument rather than a talking point. You've hands-on deployed LLM-based workflows, automation, and AI-assisted analytics to cut manual effort out of repeatable commercial tasks, and you're genuinely energized by evaluating new tools and figuring out how to make them stick for people with very different levels of technical comfort.

This role sits at the intersection of Lean rigor, commercial strategy, and applied AI, working in close partnership with the VP of GTM Operations, market leaders, Strategic Account Managers, the deal desk, and the Enterprise Lean Team. You'll have real latitude to identify where the organization's commercial processes are breaking down, design the "least waste way" to fix them, and build the institutional memory that keeps the organization improving — treating every gap as a system problem to solve, not people problem to handle.

What you get to do

  • Identify commercial process gaps across sales, business development, and deal execution, and design best-in-class workflows grounded in Lean principles and RLOS
  • Build and deploy AI-powered workflows — LLMs, automation, and AI-assisted analytics — to reduce manual effort in tasks like proposal generation, CRM hygiene, and documentation
  • Serve as the commercial team's go-to expert on practical AI applications, evaluating and recommending new tools as the landscape evolves
  • Own standard work and SOPs across the commercial organization, including governance, version control, and accessibility
  • Lead organizational change for process transformation — collaborator alignment, resistance management, and adoption planning
  • Design and deliver modular, role-specific training that drives lasting adoption, reinforced through ongoing touchpoints
  • Monitor process alignment, diagnose drift, and close gaps through coaching and refresher interventions
  • Maintain a documented evolution log and run a formal continuous improvement cadence — process reviews, retrospectives, and data-driven prioritization — reporting progress to the VP of GTM Operations

What you bring to the Team

  • Proven experience in commercial operations, GTM operations, process excellence, or a closely related function
  • Demonstrated, hands-on experience deploying AI tools (LLMs, automation platforms, AI-assisted analytics) in a commercial or operational context
  • Working knowledge of Lean methodologies — value stream mapping, standard work, root cause analysis, PDCA — applied in a commercial or non-manufacturing environment
  • Experience building SOPs and standard work documentation at an organizational scale
  • Strong facilitation and training skills, with comfort delivering to mixed-experience audiences
  • Analytical fluency, with the ability to use data to diagnose process problems and measure improvement outcomes

Preferred

  • Background in a PE-backed industrial, manufacturing, or multi-site commercial environment

title: Senior Security Researcher
excerpt: About UsAI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.
description:
About Us

AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and exploited, then delivers fixes that won’t break the application. Security teams get evidence instead of noise, and developers get fixes instead of tickets.

The companies building AI trust us to secure it - our customers include OpenAI, SpaceX, DoorDash, Dropbox, Atlassian, MongoDB, Snowflake, Robinhood and Peloton to name a few.

Endor Labs is the third company from Founder & CEO Varun Badhwar, who built Prisma Cloud, the platform that helped define cloud security, from $0 to $300M ARR at Palo Alto Networks. We’ve raised $163M from Lightspeed, Coatue, DFJ Growth, Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital.

Software runs everything around our lives today - banking, hospitals, airports and power grids. AI now writes more of it every day, and our mission is to make sure the world can trust that software. Come build that future with us.

About the Role

We are looking for a Senior Security Researcher to join in our offensive security research efforts in the domain of software supply chain security. This is a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of secure SDLC and software supply chain security, identifying zero-day vulnerabilities in software artifacts and CI/CD systems, analyzing attack trends, and influencing the next generation of security capabilities in our products.

This role requires deep technical expertise in vulnerability research, application security, reverse engineering, and offensive security techniques. The ideal candidate will also play a key role in publishing groundbreaking research through blogs, white papers, and speaking engagements at top security conferences.

How You'll Make an Impact

  • Conduct offensive security research on software supply chain threats, identifying and analyzing zero-day vulnerabilities.
  • Develop and refine exploit techniques to understand modern attack vectors targeting software supply chain through malicious code, 3rd party libraries, and CI/CD systems.
  • Work closely with Product Management to translate research findings into innovative security capabilities within Endor Labs' products.
  • Publish research findings through technical blogs, white papers, and industry-leading security conferences.
  • Collaborate with security engineers and developers to prototype and implement detection and mitigation strategies for emerging threats.
  • Contribute to the security community by developing open-source tools, methodologies, or frameworks that enhance software supply chain security.
  • Stay ahead of the latest threats, attacker methodologies, and evolving security trends to continuously refine our research efforts.

What You Bring to the Table

  • 5+ years of experience in security research, vulnerability discovery, and offensive security.
  • Deep expertise in reverse engineering, exploit development, and software vulnerability analysis.
  • Strong understanding of software supply chain security, including package management systems, CI/CD pipelines, and dependency analysis.
  • Experience discovering and responsibly disclosing zero-day vulnerabilities.
  • Proven track record of publishing high-quality research or presenting at top security conferences (e.g., Black Hat, DEF CON, RSAC, BSides).
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Rust, or Go.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to conduct complex security research autonomously.
  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, to convey technical concepts to diverse audiences.

Why Endor Labs

We’re building at the intersection of developer productivity and security — one of the fastest-growing spaces in software. Our dev-loved platform has real ROI, strong momentum, and customers who care about doing things right. You get to work with a world-class team dedicated to pushing the boundaries of security research and directly influence the security of modern software supply chains.

At Endor Labs, we think big, start small, and learn fast. We take ownership, move with purpose, and always start with the customer’s success. We debate with data, make the complex simple, and challenge each other with kindness and candor. We celebrate wins, learn from misses, and have fun along the way — because when our customers win, we all win.

Endor Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Even if you don't fit every requirement above, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and experiences, so we encourage all talented individuals to apply—there's no one-size-fits-all here.

description:
Job Type:Full Time | Location:Texas | Department: Innovation | Reporting to:Chief Innovation Officer | Work Location Type: #remote

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

The Principal Engineer, Mechanical Innovationis IREN's subject matter expert in mechanical and HVAC engineering within the Innovation organization, reporting to the VP, Mechanical Innovation. This role operates at the intersection of innovation and execution — translating the mechanical engineering standards and architectural concepts developed by the Innovation team into practical designs and technical guidance that project teams can act on.

The Principal Engineer works directly with the NGDC and IMDC project engineers to execute new designs, ensures cross-discipline alignment with electrical, Next-Gen Data Center, and Industrialized Manufacturing programs, and serves as a technical resource to IREN's broader engineering, construction, and commissioning organizations.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

Responsibilities

Mechanical & HVAC Engineering — Subject Matter Expertise
  • Serve as IREN's internal subject matter expert in mechanical and HVAC engineering — providing authoritative technical guidance on air-side cooling systems, cooling distribution, fluid systems, thermal management, computational fluid dynamics (CFD), and mechanical plant design for next-generation and industrialized data center infrastructure.
  • Develop and maintain mechanical engineering design deliverables within the Innovation program, including cooling system layouts, equipment schedules, fluid system schematics, CFD analyses, thermal performance models, and design basis documents that establish IREN's technical standards for mechanical systems.
  • Evaluate emerging mechanical and HVAC technologies, equipment, and methodologies — providing technically grounded recommendations to the VP, Mechanical Innovation on opportunities to improve thermal performance, system efficiency, and deployability across IREN's infrastructure portfolio.
Design Execution — NGDC & IMDC Programs
  • Partner directly with the NGDC and IMDC project engineers to translate Innovation-developed mechanical standards and architectural concepts into executable designs — providing hands-on technical support through design development, review, and resolution of complex mechanical and thermal system issues.
  • Review and provide technical approval of mechanical designs, calculations, and specifications produced by NGDC and IMDC project teams, ensuring alignment with Innovation standards and identifying deviations that require resolution before designs are released for procurement or construction.
  • Support the development of mechanical systems within IREN's modular and prefabricated assemblies — including cooling distribution units, mechanical skids, and prefabricated fluid handling systems — providing mechanical engineering expertise through design, factory acceptance testing, and field commissioning.
Cross-Discipline Coordination
  • Ensure mechanical and HVAC designs are coordinated with the electrical team — resolving interdependencies between cooling systems, power distribution, and thermal loads at the design stage to prevent field conflicts and ensure integrated system performance.
  • Maintain active technical alignment with the NGDC and IMDC programs — participating in design reviews, interface meetings, and technical workshops to ensure that mechanical decisions made within each program are consistent with Innovation standards and do not create downstream conflicts across disciplines or projects.
  • Identify and escalate cross-discipline interface issues — including mechanical-to-electrical, mechanical-to-structural, and mechanical-to-controls conflicts — to the VP, Mechanical Innovation with clear technical framing and recommended resolution paths.
Support to Engineering, Construction & Commissioning
  • Serve as a technical resource to IREN's engineering, construction, and commissioning teams on mechanical and HVAC matters — responding to RFIs, supporting design clarifications, reviewing submittals, and providing field technical support for complex mechanical installations.
  • Support commissioning activities for mechanical systems — including review of commissioning plans, participation in functional testing and thermal performance validation, troubleshooting of HVAC and fluid system anomalies, and documentation of as-commissioned performance against design intent.
  • Capture field learnings and construction observations, feeding technically validated lessons back into Innovation's mechanical engineering standards to continuously improve design quality and reduce rework on future projects.
Standards & Documentation
  • Contribute to the development and maintenance of IREN's mechanical engineering standards library — authoring and updating design criteria, equipment specifications, and calculation templates for cooling and fluid systems in alignment with applicable codes (ASHRAE, SMACNA, ASME, NFPA) and IREN-specific requirements.
  • Produce clear, complete technical documentation for all mechanical engineering deliverables — ensuring that design intent, thermal assumptions, and interface requirements are captured in a form that enables downstream teams to execute accurately without requiring further interpretation.

Requirements

  • 12+ years of progressive mechanical engineering experience with deep specialization in HVAC and cooling systems — including air-side cooling design, cooling distribution, fluid system engineering, thermal modeling, and CFD analysis — within data center, mission-critical, energy, or industrial infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated experience developing mechanical engineering design deliverables — cooling system layouts, fluid schematics, equipment schedules, CFD studies, and design basis documents — at a level of technical depth and completeness suitable for direct use in construction and procurement.
  • Experience working across both innovation/development and project execution environments — able to develop standards and design concepts in a research context and apply them practically within the constraints of active construction projects.
  • Strong cross-discipline collaboration skills with the ability to coordinate mechanical decisions with electrical, structural, controls, and construction stakeholders; clear and precise technical communication, both written and verbal.
  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering required; PE registration preferred. Hyperscale or owner-operator data center experience highly valued. Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required (estimated 20–35%).

Benefits

At IREN, we offer a highly competitive compensation package that includes base salary, annual performance incentives, and opportunities to build long-term wealth through equity programs. These offerings are part of our broader total rewards package, thoughtfully designed to support your health, well-being, and long-term success.
Compensation
  • Actual compensation will be determined based on factors such as experience, qualifications, and market data for the region.
  • Total Compensation package may be inclusive of annual incentive bonus, equity (long-term incentive).
Health & Wellness
  • 100% company paid health insurance premiums (medical, dental, and vision) for employees, 75% company paid coverage for dependents
  • Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance

title: Sr AI Architect/Engineer
excerpt: An extraordinarily talented group of individuals work together every day to drive TNS' success, from both professional and personal perspectives.
description:
An extraordinarily talented group of individuals work together every day to drive TNS' success, from both professional and personal perspectives.Come join the excellence!

Overview

Researches, designs, plans, develops and/or evaluates new, advanced network technologies by translating customer requirements or strategic business objectives into final product design. Work typically includes in-depth assessment of the customer’s networked application needs, providing network modeling and simulation testing, consulting to further clarify needs, and engineering high-speed technology network transports to deliver application functionality.

Responsibilities

Why this role exists

TNS is moving from AI governance and foundations into execution. The platform building blocks are in place or underway — Microsoft 365, Copilot, Entra ID, SharePoint, and Anthropic's Claude models via AWS Bedrock. What we don't yet have is a dedicated person who can both build and operate the secure, production-grade AI platform that lets AI work safely against our dataandembed with our lines of business to turn that capability into measurable value.

This role does both. You'll be the technical engine and the on-the-ground partner who makes AI a productive, trusted tool across the enterprise — and who multiplies that impact by enabling others to build, not just building yourself.

What you'll do

Your time will span two connected halves.

Build and operate the AI platform

Model platform and private hosting. Own our Claude deployment on AWS Bedrock end to end — model access and versioning, region and data-residency decisions, provisioned throughput vs. on-demand, and the private, VPC-isolated hosting posture that keeps our data inside our boundary and out of third-party training. Evaluate and manage additional models where they fit, and maintain a routing layer so applications aren't hard-wired to a single model or provider.

Harness and orchestration management. Build and maintain the application harness that sits between our users and the models: prompt and context management, tool and function calling, agent orchestration, retrieval pipelines, guardrails and content filtering, caching, and fallback behavior. Own the evaluation harness too — regression suites, quality benchmarks, and the release process that lets us upgrade models without breaking what's in production.

Data connectivity. Design and build secure, governed connections between AI systems and TNS data — Microsoft 365 and Graph, SharePoint, databases, data warehouses, APIs, and line-of-business systems. Own the retrieval architecture, indexing and freshness strategy, and the permission-trimming that ensures every user sees only what they're entitled to see, with no leakage across boundaries.

Security and access control. Architect least-privilege access across identity, network, and data layers — IAM and Entra ID, private networking, encryption and key management, secrets handling, and tenant isolation. Defend against AI-specific threats: prompt injection, data exfiltration through model outputs, insecure tool use, and over-permissioned agents. Partner with security and governance so every deployment is auditable and compliant by design, with a full audit trail of prompts, outputs, and data access.

Monitoring and observability. Instrument the platform for production operations — latency, error rates, throughput and quota headroom, output quality and drift, guardrail trips, and anomalous usage. Build the dashboards and alerting that let us find problems before users do, and the usage telemetry that tells us which solutions are actually delivering value.

Cost management. Own AI spend as a first-class engineering concern: token-level cost attribution by application and line of business, budgets and alerting, model right-sizing (using the cheapest model that meets the quality bar), prompt caching and context optimization, batch processing where latency allows, and provisioned-throughput decisions. Produce the chargeback and unit-economics reporting leadership needs to fund the portfolio with confidence.

Reusable foundations. Turn all of the above into patterns, templates, and guardrails so each new use case is faster, cheaper, and safer to build than the last.

Ship value with the business (forward-deployed engineering)

  • Embed directly with teams across our lines of business (Communications, Waypoint, Payments, Corporate/Shared) to identify high-value AI and automation opportunities.

  • Prototype quickly, validate with real users, and take the strongest ideas to production.

  • Drive adoption — measure whether solutions are actually used and delivering value, and iterate until they are.

  • Enable others: seed and support a network of "AI champions" in each line of business, equipping non-specialists to build their own automations on your patterns and under appropriate oversight.

What you'll accomplish in your first year

  • Stand up a secure, monitored, cost-managed AI platform on AWS Bedrock with governed connectivity to TNS data.

  • Ship a portfolio of production use cases with documented, measurable value — reduced cost to serve, shorter cycle times, and volume absorbed without added headcount.

  • Establish a use-case intake and prioritization process so demand is triaged by value rather than by who asks loudest.

  • Deliver AI cost transparency and attribution by application and line of business.

  • Enable at least one capable AI champion in each line of business.

What you bring (required)

  • Strong software / solutions engineering background with hands-on experience building and deploying production AI/LLM applications — RAG, agents, tool use, orchestration, and evaluation.

  • Direct experience with a managed model platform in production; AWS Bedrock strongly preferred, along with the surrounding AWS estate (IAM, VPC, KMS, CloudWatch, PrivateLink).

  • Demonstrated ability to build and operate data connectivity to enterprise systems with permission-aware retrieval.

  • Working command of enterprise security and data governance: identity and access, data protection, encryption and key management, and AI-specific threat models.

  • Production operations instincts — you instrument what you build, and you've owned the monitoring and on-call reality of a live system.

  • Cost discipline: you treat inference spend as an engineering constraint and can show where the money goes.

  • Genuine business fluency and communication skills — you're comfortable sitting with finance, operations, or sales, understanding their problems, and translating them into solutions.

  • A demonstrated bias toward shipping and adoption, not just building demos.

Nice to have

  • Depth in the Microsoft / Azure ecosystem alongside AWS (Azure AI, Copilot Studio, Power Platform, Entra ID, SharePoint / Graph) — our environment spans both.

  • Experience in a regulated or security-sensitive industry — payments, telecom, or financial data.

  • Self-hosted or fine-tuned model experience, and a clear view of when it beats a managed API.

  • Infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD for AI systems (Terraform, pipelines, automated evals in the release path).

  • Change-management or internal-consulting experience.

  • Prior forward-deployed or customer-facing engineering experience.

Qualifications

Who you are

The rare blend of builder and partner. You carry the technical depth of a staff engineer and the people instincts of an internal consultant. You're energized by variety — a private-networking and key-management problem in the morning, a finance-team workflow in the afternoon. You measure yourself by value delivered and adopted, not lines of code. You teach and multiply rather than hoard knowledge. And you operate with ownership: when a deployment is struggling or a cost-line spikes, you own the fix.

How your success is measured

In short: reduced cost to serve on named processes, use cases shipped and sustained in production, adoption across lines of business, champions enabled, platform reliability and cost-per-unit-of-value, and a clean security and governance record.


For this role, we anticipate paying $150,000 - $250,000 annually. Any compensation range provided for a role is an estimate determined by available market data. The actual amount may be higher or lower than the range provided considering each candidate’s knowledge, skills, abilities, and geographic location. TNS offers a competitive benefit package including medical and dental coverage, life insurance, paid holidays and vacations, and a 401K plan with company match.

If you are passionate about technology, love personal growth and opportunity, come see what TNS is all about!

Use your gas industry expertise to make a real difference to public safety, industry standards and the reputation of Gas Safe Register.

We are looking for an experienced gas professional to join the Gas Safe Register team as a Technical Support Officer. This is a home-working role and an excellent opportunity to move into a trusted technical advisory position where your knowledge, judgement and communication skills will help support registered businesses, stakeholders and members of the public.

In this role, you will provide clear, accurate and practical technical information on gas safety, associated building industries and ACS-related matters. You will play an important part in helping people understand their responsibilities, supporting compliance with relevant legislation and promoting safe standards across the gas industry.

Job title:

Gas Technical support Officer

Job Description:

About Gas Safe Register

Gas Safe Register is the official gas registration body for the United Kingdom, Isle of Man, Jersey and Guernsey. By law, gas businesses and engineers must be registered to carry out gas work legally. The register helps protect the public from unsafe gas work by maintaining the official list of competent businesses and engineers, supporting inspections, investigating safety concerns and raising awareness of gas safety standards.

Capita delivers the Gas Safe Register service under a concession arrangement with the Health and Safety Executive and related authorities. Together, we help maintain gas safety standards and give consumers confidence that gas work is carried out safely, legally and professionally.

Why Join Us?

  • Use your technical gas experience in a role focused on advice, guidance and public protection.
  • Move into a varied support role where no two enquiries are the same.
  • Influence safety awareness by helping stakeholders, gas businesses and the public understand key requirements.
  • Contribute to technical publications, guidance and bulletins that support the wider industry.
  • Join a service with a clear purpose: helping improve and maintain gas safety standards across the UK.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Respond to telephone, written and email enquiries from stakeholders, registered businesses and the general public, providing clear and professional technical guidance.
  • Provide information and advice on gas safety, associated building industries and Nationally Accredited Certification Scheme for Individual Gas Fitting Operatives (ACS) matters.
  • Support other Gas Safe Register departments with accurate technical guidance to help ensure compliance with relevant legislation and industry standards.
  • Research, write, review and edit technical articles, publications and bulletins, ensuring information is accurate, consistent and easy to understand.
  • Keep up to date with industry changes, technical standards and legislation so that advice remains current and reliable.
  • Provide cover and support across technical areas when required, helping maintain high service standards.
  • Promote Gas Safe Register positively across the gas industry, associated trades and the general public.

What We’re Looking For

This role would suit an experienced gas industry professional who enjoys sharing knowledge, solving technical queries and communicating clearly with a wide range of people. You will be confident interpreting technical information, making sound decisions and providing advice that supports compliance, safety and strong customer service.

Essential Requirements

  • A minimum of eight years’ experience working within the gas industry.
  • City & Guilds, NVQ or equivalent qualification in gas service engineering.
  • Appropriate ACS proof of competence.
  • Broad knowledge of the gas industry and related technical standards.
  • Excellent understanding of health and safety, Building Regulations and other relevant legislation.
  • Strong customer service skills, with the ability to explain technical information clearly and professionally.
  • Ability to gather information, research topics and use evidence to support effective decision making.
  • Strong prioritisation, organisation and time management skills, with the ability to work under pressure.
  • Good knowledge and confidence using computer-based systems.

What’s in It for You?

  • A role where your experience is valued and used to support safer gas standards.
  • £41,000 annual salary
  • The flexibility of a home-working role, allowing you to use your technical expertise in a professional support environment.
  • The opportunity to step away from hands-on engineering while staying connected to the industry.
  • Varied technical work, including advisory support, research, publications and stakeholder engagement.
  • A professional environment where accuracy, knowledge and good judgement make a meaningful impact.
  • Career development opportunities across Capita, with support to build skills and progress your career.

Ready to Apply?

If you are an experienced gas professional looking to use your technical knowledge in a role with purpose, variety and real public safety impact, we would welcome your application. This is a great opportunity to support the wider gas industry, help improve safety awareness and be part of a trusted national service.

excerpt: Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and succeed in the AI-driven content era.
description:
Storyblok is a headless CMS that enables marketers and developers to create with joy and succeed in the AI-driven content era. It empowers you to deliver structured and consistent content everywhere: websites, apps, AI search, and beyond.

Marketers get a visual editor with reusable components, in-context preview, and workflows to launch fast and stay on brand. Legendary brands like Virgin Media O2, Oatly, and TomTom use Storyblok to make a bigger, faster market impact. It’s Joyful Headless™, and it changes everything.

WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU

You will be joining a growing company where you can contribute to many “firsts”. Plus these benefits:

  • Monthly remote work stipend (home internet costs, electricity). Home office equipment package right at the start (laptop, keyboard, monitor…)
  • Home office equipment upgrade (furniture, ear plugs …) or membership to a local co-working space after your onboarding
  • Sick leave benefit, parental leave and 25 days of annual leave plus your local national holidays
  • Personal development fund for courses, books, conferences, and material
  • VSOP (Virtual Stock Option Plan)
  • The annual international team-building trip, quarterly and monthly online get-togethers
  • As a fully remote company, with work-life balance at its core, you’ll enjoy flexible schedules
  • An international team that loves to have fun at work and works hard together to accomplish shared goals

JOB SUMMARY

We’re looking for a Senior QA Engineer who combines strong Playwright and TypeScript engineering skills with a proactive, collaborative mindset. You'll be a key contributor to how we deliver quality, raising the bar for our automation codebase and partnering closely with engineering to define how testing responsibility is shared across the team.

You’ll join our dynamic and growing Product Engineering team at Storyblok, playing an instrumental role in ensuring the quality and reliability of our flagship CMS platform. This platform empowers businesses to create and deliver seamless digital content experiences.

In this role, you'll work closely with product owners, designers, and developers to design and maintain clean, scalable, well-architected TypeScript automation, establish clear guidelines on which test level is right for a given change, and continuously refine QA strategies to maintain best-in-class software quality. Your work will directly contribute to delivering an exceptional user experience by ensuring flawless performance across every facet of our application.


ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS

  • Own projects end-to-end with clarity, technical excellence, and accountability, ensuring high-quality standards across teams.
  • Champion strong TypeScript engineering practices and coding standards across the QA codebase, promoting engineering excellence and driving continuous improvement.
  • Design, implement, and maintain efficient, well-typed, and reliable automated tests across frontend and backend using Playwright.
  • Raise the team's TypeScript bar: introduce stronger typing patterns, reusable abstractions, linting/tooling standards, and code review practices that improve maintainability across the automation codebase.
  • Partner with engineering to define, implement, and enforce the test pyramid in practice, establishing clear guidelines on which test level (unit, integration, E2E) is appropriate for a given change, and driving adoption so both developers and QAs consistently write tests at the right level.
  • Perform manual and exploratory testing; document, track, and verify defects to ensure product excellence and analyze test results and monitor key testing metrics to identify patterns and opportunities for improvement.
  • Participate actively in project kick-offs to understand requirements, anticipate risks, and influence testability from the earliest stages.
  • Identify and communicate issues, risks, or dependencies early, escalating to product leadership when necessary.
  • Mentor and support teammates on TypeScript proficiency and Playwright best practices, fostering an open, empathetic environment that encourages learning and feedback.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • 7+ years of relevant experience as a QA Engineer or Software Engineer in Test.
  • Deep proficiency in TypeScript, including a strong command of advanced typing and code architecture, as well as Playwright.
  • Practical experience partnering with engineers to define and roll out test pyramid guidelines, including setting expectations for which test level is appropriate and holding both developers and QAs accountable for following them.
  • Comprehensive knowledge of CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions) and experience creating and maintaining containerized test environments.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence and align across technical and product teams.
  • High attention to detail, proven ability to deliver results, and a strong motivation to contribute to organizational growth in a high-performing environment.
  • Experience mentoring engineers, defining and driving TypeScript and test automation standards across teams.
  • Demonstrates AI literacy, with the ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, decision-making, and quality of work while applying sound judgment and critical thinking.

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience writing and maintaining Ruby on Rails code.
  • Experience with observability and error tracking tools (eg. Grafana, Kibana, Sentry) and identifying errors, trends, and issues.
  • Experience with performance testing and best practices.

MENTAL, PHYSICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL REQUIREMENTS

Remote (home) work opportunity or funded by Storyblok co-working space
